title: Atrial fibrillation: oral anticoagulant selection
scope: Week 02, atrial fibrillation. One selected guideline document and one directly cited primary study. Research-stage educational draft; not clinically approved or a treatment directive.

documents.highlight: For atrial fibrillation patients who are candidates for anticoagulation and have neither moderate-to-severe rheumatic mitral stenosis nor a mechanical heart valve, the 2023 ACC/AHA/ACCP/HRS guideline recommends a direct oral anticoagulant rather than warfarin (Class 1, Level A).
documents.locator: Section 6.3.1, Antithrombotic Therapy, recommendation 2 (COR 1, LOE A); supporting references 1-7; section-specific bibliography reference 3 is Granger et al. (ARISTOTLE).
documents.x1_linkage_status: direct_primary_trial_citation_verified_for_apixaban_vs_warfarin; single trial is not sufficient to establish a class-wide conclusion

x1.linkage_note: The guideline directly cites ARISTOTLE as reference 3 under Section 6.3.1 recommendation 2. This trial is direct primary evidence for one DOAC (apixaban) versus warfarin, not the entire DOAC class; other trials also support the class recommendation.

picot.P: 18,201 patients with atrial fibrillation and at least one additional risk factor for stroke; patients with moderate/severe mitral stenosis or mechanical prosthetic valves were not the indicated population.
picot.I: Apixaban 5 mg twice daily (dose-reduction rules applied to eligible patients in trial).
picot.O: Stroke or systemic embolism: 1.27%/year with apixaban vs 1.60%/year with warfarin, HR 0.79 (95% CI 0.66-0.95); major bleeding: 2.13%/year vs 3.09%/year, HR 0.69 (0.60-0.80); all-cause death HR 0.89 (0.80-0.99).
picot.T: Median follow-up 1.8 years; randomized, double-blind noninferiority trial with superiority testing.

x1.limitations: Supports apixaban specifically, not every available DOAC; trial eligibility, renal function, drug interactions, adherence, hemorrhage risk and patient-specific contraindications require independent clinical evaluation. Industry funded.
